extracted.intended_audience: users/developers of SINGULAR/polymake tropical.lib (computational algebra / tropical geometry practitioners writing SINGULAR scripts)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in the tropical.lib library of SINGULAR: usage signatures, assumptions, return values, notes and examples for functions used in tropical geometry computations and TeX output generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: initialForm
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: initialForm(f,w); f a polynomial, w an integer vector. Assume: f is a polynomial in Q[x1,...,xn] and w=(w1,...,wn). Return: poly, the initial form of f(x) w.r.t. w. Note: the initialForm consists of the terms with MAXIMAL weighted order w.r.t. w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shown: for f = x^3 + y^2 - x y + x - 1 and w = (2,3) initialForm(f,w) returns x^3 + y^2. (Keep in mind weighted order; selects maximal-weight terms.)

rubrics_metrics.name: initialIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: initialIdeal(i,w); i ideal, w intvec. Assume: i is an ideal in Q[x1,...,xn] and w=(w1,...,wn). Return: ideal, the initialIdeal of i w.r.t. w. Note: the initialIdeal consists of the terms with MAXIMAL weighted order w.r.t. w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: initialIdeal called on a polynomial/ideal returns the ideal consisting of initialForms of generators (terms of maximal weighted order). Example output printed shows generators of the initial ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: texNumber
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: texNumber(f); f poly. Return: string, TeX command representing leading coefficient of f using \frac.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: with base ring r=(0,t) calling texNumber((3t^2-1)/t^3) returns '\tfrac{-1+3\cdot t^{2}}{t^{3}}'.

rubrics_metrics.name: texPolynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: texPolynomial(f); f poly. Return: string, the TeX command representing f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: texPolynomial(1/t*x^2 - t^2*x + 1/t) returns '\tfrac{1}{t}\cdot x^{2}-t^{2}\cdot x+\tfrac{1}{t}'.

rubrics_metrics.name: texMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: texMatrix(M); M matrix. Return: string, the TeX command representing M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example builds a 2x2 matrix with polynomial entries and texMatrix(M) returns a TeX array/matrix representation (uses \left(\begin{array} ... ).

rubrics_metrics.name: texDrawBasic
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: texDrawBasic(texdraw); list texdraw. Assume: texdraw is a list of strings representing texdraw commands (as produced by texDrawTropical) which should be embedded into a texdraw environment. Return: string, a texdraw environment enclosing the input. Note: is called from conicWithTangents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: texDrawBasic wraps generated texdraw code in '\begin{texdraw}' ... '\end{texdraw}', includes drawing setup commands (\drawdim, \relunitscale, etc.) and lattice code. Useful to embed texdraw commands into a complete environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: texDrawTropical
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: texDrawTropical(graph[,#]); graph list, # optional list. Assume: graph is the output of tropicalCurve. Return: string, the texdraw code of the tropical plane curve encoded by graph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: if # is non-empty, first entry may be 'max' to consider curve with respect to maximum; procedure computes a scalefactor (which may be undesirable when assembling multiple outputs) and scalefactor can be prescribed via optional poly entry; last optional string can insert further texdraw commands; # may be empty. Examples show produced texdraw commands and optional scalefactor usage (texDrawTropical(graph,"",1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: texDrawNewtonSubdivision
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: texDrawNewtonSubdivision(graph[,#]); graph list, # optional list. Assume: graph is the output of tropicalCurve. Return: string, the texdraw code of the Newton subdivision of the tropical plane curve encoded by graph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: optional list # may contain a poly specifying scaling factor (first poly-type entry); if missing factor is computed. Lattice points black = marked in marked subdivision, grey = unmarked. Example shows TeX draw output including lattice points and marking.

rubrics_metrics.name: texDrawTriangulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: texDrawTriangulation(triang,polygon); triang,polygon list. Assume: polygon is a list of integer vectors describing lattice points of a marked polygon; triang is a list describing a triangulation where an integer vector (i,j,k) describes the triangle formed by polygon[i], polygon[j], polygon[k]. Return: string, a texdraw code for the triangulation described by triang without the texdraw environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs polygon as list of integer points and triang as list of triples; returns texdraw commands for triangulation drawing, vertices and markers.

rubrics_metrics.name: radicalMemberShip
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: radicalMemberShip(f,i); f poly, i ideal. Return: int, 1 if f is in the radical of i, 0 else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows behavior depends on ordering: with global ordering y is NOT in radical of i=(x+1)*y^2 -> returns 0; with local ordering (ds) y is in radical -> returns 1. So result depends on ring ordering context.

rubrics_metrics.name: tInitialFormPar
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tInitialFormPar(f,w); f a polynomial, w an integer vector. Assume: f is a polynomial in Q(t)[x1,...,xn] and w=(w1,...,w2). Return: poly, the t-initialform of f(t,x) w.r.t. (1,w) evaluated at t=1. Note: the t-initialform are the terms with MINIMAL weighted order w.r.t. (1,w).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for f=t^4 x^2 + y^2 - t^2 x y + t^4 x - t^9 and w=(2,3) tInitialFormPar(f,w) returns y^2 + x (after evaluation at t=1 selecting minimal weighted order terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: tInitialFormParMax
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tInitialFormParMax(f,w); f a polynomial, w an integer vector. Assume: f is a polynomial in Q(t)[x1,...,xn] and w=(w1,...,w2). Return: poly, the t-initialform of f(t,x) w.r.t. (-1,w) evaluated at t=1. Note: the t-initialform are the terms with MAXIMAL weighted order w.r.t. (1,w).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: with f having 1/t^6 term and w=(2,3), tInitialFormParMax returns y^2 - 1 (selects maximal weighted order terms after substituting -1 weight on t).

rubrics_metrics.name: solveTInitialFormPar
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: solveTInitialFormPar(i); i ideal. Assume: i is a zero-dimensional ideal in Q(t)[x1,...,xn] generated by the (1,w)-homogeneous elements for some integer vector w (i.e. by the (1,w)-initialforms of polynomials). Return: none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: the procedure displays complex approximations of the solution set of i. Example output shows complex approximate solutions and formatting messages about number of variables and ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: detropicalise
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: detropicalise(f); f poly or f list. Assume: if f is poly then t is a linear polynomial with an arbitrary constant term and positive integer coefficients as further coefficients; if f is list then it's a list of polynomials of that type. Return: poly, the detropicalisation of f ignoring the constant parts. Note: the output will be a monomial and the constant coefficient has been ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: detropicalise(3x+4y-1) returns x^3 y^4 (monomial formed from linear polynomial coefficients, constant ignored).

rubrics_metrics.name: tDetropicalise
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tDetropicalise(f); f poly or f list. Assume: if f is poly then f is a linear polynomial with an integer constant term and positive integer coefficients as further coefficients; if f is list then it is a list of such polynomials. Return: poly, the detropicalisation of f over the field Q(t). Note: the output will be a term where the coefficient is a Laurent monomial in t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: tDetropicalise(3x+4y-1) returns 1/(t)*x^3 y^4 (coefficient is a Laurent monomial in t).

rubrics_metrics.name: dualConic
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dualConic(f); f poly. Assume: f is an affine conic in two variables x and y. Return: poly, the equation of the dual conic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for conic = 2x^2 + 1/2 y^2 - 1, dualConic(conic) returns 1/2 x^2 + 2 y^2 - 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: parameterSubstitute
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: parameterSubstitute(f,N); f poly, N int. Assume: f is a polynomial in Q(t)[x1,...,xn] describing a plane curve over Q(t). Return: poly f with t replaced by t^N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: parameterSubstitute(f,3) replaces t by t^3; parameterSubstitute(f,-1) replaces t by t^{-1} producing Laurent powers accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: tropicalSubst
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: parameterSubstitute(f,N,L); f poly, N int, L list. (Note: text shows this as 'tropicalSubst' earlier.) Assume: f is a polynomial in Q(t)[x1,...,xk] and L is a list of the form var(i1),poly1,...,var(ik),polyk. Return: list, the tropical polynomial obtained from f by replacing the i-th variable by the i-th polynomial but in that polynomial the parameter t is replaced by t^{1/N}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate usage to study transformations x -> x + t^b and effects on tropicalisation and j-invariant of a cubic over Puiseux series; shows optional behaviors and how genus/cycle length/j-invariant computations follow. Also shows warnings about integer division in SINGULAR scripts ('use div instead').

rubrics_metrics.name: randomPolyInT
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: randomPolyInT(d,ug,og[,#]); d, ug, og int, # list. Assume: the base ring has a parameter t. Return: poly, a polynomial of degree d where the coefficients are of the form t^j with j a random integer between ug and og.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: if optional argument # is given, coefficients may be either t^j or zero chosen randomly. Examples show generated polynomials with Laurent monomial coefficients and optional sparsity when fourth argument present.

rubrics_metrics.name: cleanTmp
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: cleanTmp(). Purpose: some procedures create LaTeX and PS files in /tmp; calling cleanTmp() removes them. Return: none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to remove temporary files produced by tex-related procedures (texDraw..., etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: groebnerCone
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: groebnerCone(I,w); I ideal or poly, w intvec or bigintmat. Assume: I a reduced standard basis and w contained in the maximal Groebner cone. Return: cone, the Groebner cone of I with respect to w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: compute reduced standard basis stdI of ideal I, choose w inside maximal Groebner cone and get cone CwI = groebnerCone(stdI,w); then inspect rays(CwI). Behavior shown for w in interior, on facet, or on ray of maximal cone with different printed ray sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: maximalGroebnerCone
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: maximalGroebnerCone(I); I ideal or poly. Assume: I a reduced standard basis. Return: cone, the maximal Groebner cone of I with respect to the current ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show computing maximal Groebner cone for stdI and for homogenized ideals; print rays and generatorsOfLinealitySpace to inspect cone structure; works with different rings and orderings.

rubrics_metrics.name: homogeneitySpace
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: homogeneitySpace(I); I ideal or poly. Assume: I a reduced standard basis. Return: cone, the set of all weight vectors with respect to whom I is weighted homogeneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: homogeneitySpace(stdI) then print(generatorsOfLinealitySpace(C0I)). For homogenized ideal, prints a generator like -1,-1,-1,-1 indicating lineality of homogeneity space.

rubrics_metrics.name: initial
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: initial(f,w); f poly, w intvec or bigintmat.       initial(I,w); I ideal, w intvec or bigintmat. Assume: I reduced Groebner basis, w in the maximal Groebner cone of I with respect to the current ordering. Return: poly or ideal, the initial form of f or the initial ideal of I with respect to w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for stdI computed from cyclic(3) and w=(1,1,1), initial(stdI,w) returns an ideal where some generators have constants removed (e.g., z^3-1 becomes z^3). Use when w is in maximal Groebner cone; relies on reduced Groebner basis assumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: tropicalVariety
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tropicalVariety(f[,p]); f poly, p optional number.       tropicalVariety(I[,p]); I ideal, p optional number. Assume: I homogeneous, p prime number. Return: fan, the tropical variety of f resp. I with respect to the trivial valuation or the p-adic valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: set printlevel=1 for output during traversal. Examples show output as a PolyhedralFan application with fields AMBIENT_DIM, DIM, LINEALITY_DIM, RAYS, N_RAYS, LINEALITY_SPACE, ORTH_LINEALITY_SPACE, F_VECTOR, SIMPLICIAL, PURE, CONES, MAXIMAL_CONES etc. Providing an optional prime number p computes tropical variety with respect to p-adic valuation and changes ambient dimension and cones accordingly.
